Alex —

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team (cc'd) ran a redline and flagged a few material items around indemnity for third-party IP claims and the evidence/notice procedures. I attached our redline (CedarTech_MSA_Redline_v2.pdf). High-level asks:

- Can Redwood confirm whether indemnity covers third-party claims alleging infringement caused by Redwood's hosted model outputs (not customer-provided models)?
- We want clear notice/evidence obligations and a short SLA for Redwood to accept/deny a claim (we propose 10 business days).
- On defense control: CedarTech prefers to retain control where we deem it necessary for regulatory matters; otherwise we expect Redwood to take lead on defense for claims relating to the underlying model.

Attached is a list of evidence items we will likely request (CedarTech_Request_Evidence_List.txt). Please let us know if Redwood can provide those items in a standard response (log snippets, sample prompt/response where available, dates of alleged outputs).

We'd like to keep this narrow — only third-party infringement claims, not downstream misuse or prompts. But we also need assurance about how claims tied to customer-tuned derivatives would be handled.

Could you loop in your legal? Happy to hop on a short call next week to align.

Thanks,
Susan Jones
Head of Procurement, CedarTech Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: indemnity & IP redlines attached

Hi Susan / Alex —

Thanks for the redline and the initial questions. I reviewed the proposed edits and drafted a narrower compromise that we think is operationally realistic and defensible. Key points of Redwood's proposed language (see attached proposed_indemnity_text.docx):

- Scope: Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer for third-party claims asserting that Redwood-managed model outputs (i.e., outputs produced by models that Redwood provides and manages in hosted or dedicated offerings) directly infringe a third party's intellectual property.
- Exclusions: Claims arising from (i) Customer-modified models or customer-supplied training data; (ii) Customer prompts or instructions that produce an infringing output; or (iii) Customer's combination of Redwood output with other materials that produces infringement, are excluded.
- Defense control: Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of our choice, but must consult with Customer on any settlement that materially affects Customer's rights. If Customer reasonably requests to take control for regulatory or highly sensitive matters, we can permit that, with reasonable cooperation on costs and counsel selection.
- Evidence & Notice: Customer must provide prompt written notice, and to the extent available, copies of the claim, a sample allegedly infringing output, dates/times, and any relevant request logs. Redwood will acknowledge receipt within 3 business days and provide a coverage position within 10 business days.
- Remedies/Cap: Propose liability cap aligned with Order Form fees (e.g., 12 months of fees) and standard exceptions for willful misconduct.

We think this balances operational needs with procurement's desire for clarity. If CedarTech needs alternative language around escrow, insurance thresholds, or longer notice windows, we can discuss.

Proposed next steps: 1) Confirm scope items above; 2) Agree evidence list and SLAs; 3) Contract teams finalize redlines and exchange final text.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_indemnity_text.docx (redlined proposal)

From: Susan Jones <susan.jones@cedartech.com>

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear summary and the proposed compromise. A few items from our side:

- Scope: CedarTech can accept the exclusion for customer-modified models, but we need explicit carveouts for regulatory obligations tied to patient data where we may need control of certain responses.
- Defense control: We prefer to retain the right to assume control where a claim triggers regulatory notice obligations or involves sensitive PHI — we can agree to reasonable cooperation on counsel selection and costs if we exercise that right.
- Evidence SLA: 3 business days to acknowledge and 10 business days for coverage position is acceptable; please commit to preserving relevant request logs for at least 12 months (our security/compliance team requires this).
- Cap: Would Redwood consider 18 months of recurring fees as a cap? Alternatively, can you confirm you carry insurance that would respond to these claims (carrier and limits)?

We are open to a short call to finalize. John (our counsel) is available Nov 29 — would Redwood be able to meet then?

Regards,
Susan Jones
Head of Procurement, CedarTech Health
